item.title: 【農業】 Global reallocation of rainfed crops can boost production and reduce climate risk
item.description: Spatial optimization can reduce production risk and improve output without expanding land or irrigation, but meeting future demand will require a combined strategy of global crop redistribution, yield-gap closure and stronger trade cooperation.

item.title: 【農業】 Climate change and interprovincial trade move grain production and environmental burdens northwards in China
item.description: Northward shifts in China’s grain production, driven by expanded trade and climate change, transfer environmental burdens to less affluent northern regions—a trend that is environmentally and economically unsustainable. Spatially differentiated compensation mechanisms are needed to redress these growing regional inequities

item.title: 【農業】 Limited net-export capacity undermines the Netherlands’ ‘feeding the world’ narrative
item.description: The Netherlands is one of the world’s top trading countries and the second largest exporter of agricultural goods. Using an agroecological food system model, this study examines the feasibility of this position.

item.title: 【AI4S】 Filter By:
item.description: X-ray imaging serves as a fundamental tool for non-destructive inspection. Although conventional radiography is well suited for two-dimensional imaging, it cannot provide volumetric structure. Computed tomography provides three-dimensional reconstruction but remains constrained by bulky instrumentation, high radiation exposure, and cost. Here we demonstrate a patch-type scintillator integrated with multi-stage neural network that segments and reconstructs three-dimensional volumes from sparse angular two-dimensional radiographs. The scintillator is fabricated by electrospraying cellulose nanocrystals onto a bulk cellulose matrix, followed by dip-coating of perovskite, yielding a composite with enhanced radioluminescence under X-ray excitation. This flexible film conforms to complex geometries, enabling distortion-free and multi-angle imaging. Neural networks are trained on synthetic datasets and validated on experimentally acquired avian tibiotarsus radiographs, accurately reconstructing volumetric bone structures.
